memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: They fought against Midian, as the Lord commanded Moses, and killed every man. Among their victims were Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba—the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword. The Israelites captured the Midianite women and children and took all the Midianite herds, flocks and goods as plunder. - Num 31:7-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is hard reading, and we should not pretend otherwise. Scripture does not hide the brutal cost of judgment, and honest faith does not look away from difficult passages. One name here deserves attention: Balaam. He is the prophet who could not curse Israel with his mouth, so he taught Midian to seduce Israel into sin instead (Num 31:16). His death shows that clever compromise with evil eventually catches up with a person. The New Testament remembers Balaam as a warning against those who love the rewards of wickedness (2 Pet 2:15; Jude 11).

We cannot simply transfer this event into our lives as a model for how to treat enemies. This was a unique, God-commanded act of judgment against a nation at a fixed moment, not a pattern for the church. Under the new covenant, Jesus overcame His enemies not by destroying them but by dying for them.

Yet the deeper truth remains sobering and needful: sin is deadly, and God's patience is not endless. The same God who judged Midian is the God who poured out judgment on His own Son so that we could be spared. When we feel the weight of this chapter, let it drive us not to fear but to the cross, where mercy triumphed.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "Balaam-style" compromise might be quietly working in your life?
2. Why is it important to be honest about the hard parts of the Bible rather than skipping them?
3. How does Christ bearing judgment for you deepen your gratitude?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy God, I do not always understand Your judgments, but I trust that You are just and good. Thank You that Jesus took the judgment I deserved. Keep me from every compromise with sin. Amen.
